title: The build wheel opened through the front door on both viewports: five segments, one number each, and the three ore a match starts you with
attestation: THE BOOT IS THE FRONT DOOR ON THE PRODUCTION BUNDLE (`npm run build` + `npm run preview`, /?gate=0 -> PLAY -> PLAY SOLO -> RUSH), with NO ?debug=1 and no staged ore, so there is no wheel seam under either frame and everything below is read off the pixels. The desktop wheel was opened with a real `E`; the phone wheel with a real tap at page (92,172), the centre of the `build-button` rect the client reports on that profile. The tap opened it: the frame before shows the round BUILD & UPGRADE button and no wheel, the frame after shows the wheel. WHAT IS ON THE DESKTOP FRAME. Five wedges, clockwise from twelve o'clock: TURRET, SHIELD, RADAR, REPAIR REACTOR, UPGRADE SHIP. Four build wedges carry four lines - the name, the words YOUR STATION (or YOUR SHIP), one number, and a count over its cap. TURRET: 3, `0 / 4 BUILT`. SHIELD: 5, `0 / 2 BUILT`. RADAR: 6, `0 / 1 BUILT`. REPAIR REACTOR: the second line reads REACTOR FULL instead of a target, the number is 1, and there is no count line. UPGRADE SHIP carries `OPEN` and a right-pointing triangle where the others carry a price. The hub holds a yellow `3`, the word ORE beneath it, an up-chevron, and `CLOSE . ESC`. THE ONLY NUMBERS ANYWHERE ON THE WHEEL ARE THE FOUR COSTS AND THE THREE COUNTS - no rates, no HP-per-ore, no effect text. TURRET's 3 is signal yellow; SHIELD's 5 and RADAR's 6 are threat red; REPAIR's 1 is grey. WHAT DIFFERS ON THE PHONE FRAME: the same five wedges and the same seven numbers, but the hub reads `CLOSE` with no `. ESC` - the key is not offered to a device that has none - and the count lines are set tight (`0/4 BUILT` against the desktop's `0 / 4 BUILT`). The BUILD & UPGRADE button stays drawn while the wheel is up. TWO THINGS THE PHONE FRAME SHOWS THAT ARE WRITTEN UP SEPARATELY: the pause plate that stands at the top-left when the wheel is shut is not drawn here, and the onboarding prompt band is drawn across the wheel's lower disc.

title: The wheel's cost numerals photographed at 0, 2, 3 and 6 ore: red below the price, signal yellow at it, and never one either side
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, ?debug=1, desktop 1280x800. The bank was set to 0, 2, 3 and 6 ore and the same TURRET wedge photographed at each; the four tiles on this plate are that crop at 1x, in that order. TURRET COSTS 3 IN ALL FOUR TILES - the price does not move with the purse. The NUMERAL is threat red at 0 ore and at 2 ore, and signal yellow at 3 ore and at 6 ore. It changes at exactly the price: 2 is red, 3 is yellow. The word TURRET above it is dim grey in the two red tiles and bright white in the two yellow ones, so the whole wedge and not just the numeral carries the state. The count line reads `0 / 4 BUILT` in the first three tiles and `1 / 4 BUILT` in the fourth, because the press made at the 3-ore level bought one - the levels are not independent and the fourth tile inherits the third's purchase. ONE THING ON THIS PLATE THAT IS NOT THE FINDING, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT READ AS ONE: the wedge FILL is darker in tile 1 than in tiles 2-4. That is the mouse, not the price. Tile 1 is the only frame taken before the cursor had ever been moved onto the wedge; in the other three it was still resting there from the previous level's press, and a hovered wedge is a lit wedge. THE SAME FOUR LEVELS ON THE PHONE PROFILE PRODUCE THE SAME COLOURS - red at 0 and 2, yellow at 3 and 6 - read off shots/phone-798x384-wheel-ore-*.png.

title: The developer's '2 ore built a turret' report does not reproduce - at 2 ore the press is refused and nothing is spent; at 3 ore it buys one and spends exactly three
attestation: THE VERDICT IS `verified` BECAUSE THE SCREEN IS RIGHT: the developer's reported defect could not be made to happen, and the wheel did the right thing at every level it was pressed at. PRODUCTION BUNDLE, ?debug=1. Every press below is a real click (desktop) or a real tap (phone) at the point the client itself reports drawing the TURRET wedge at: page (640,262) on desktop, (399,109) on the phone. AT 2 ORE, DESKTOP: before the press the hub reads `2 ORE`, TURRET's cost is a red 3, the count is `0 / 4 BUILT`. After the press the hub still reads `2 ORE` and the count is still `0 / 4 BUILT`. The seam agrees with the frame - bank 2 before, 2 after. Nothing was built and nothing was spent. AT 3 ORE, DESKTOP: before, hub `3 ORE`, cost a yellow 3, count `0 / 4 BUILT`. After, hub `0 ORE`, count `1 / 4 BUILT`, and the cost numeral has gone red because the emptied bank can no longer pay it. Bank 3 before, 0 after. One turret, exactly three ore. AT 0 ORE the press is likewise refused (bank 0 -> 0, count unchanged); at 6 ore it buys and leaves 3. THE PHONE PROFILE GIVES THE SAME FOUR ANSWERS at the same four levels, and its 2-ore after-frame is on this plate: hub `2 ORE`, red 3, `0/4 BUILT`. WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER: I re-priced the wheel through the ?debug=1 `setOre` seam rather than by mining, so what is proved is that the wheel and the sim agree about a bank of 2; if the reported bug needed a bank that got to 2 by some particular route - a half-collected cargo hold, a deposit mid-press - that route is not in these frames.

title: The developer's 'selection only reached the top segment' report does not reproduce - the highlight lands on every one of the five wedges, on the pointer and under a held finger
attestation: THE VERDICT IS `verified` BECAUSE THE SCREEN IS RIGHT: the developer's reported defect could not be made to happen on either profile. PRODUCTION BUNDLE, ?debug=1. DESKTOP 1280x800, TOP STRIP OF THE PLATE: a real cursor was moved onto each wedge in turn at the coordinate the client reports for it - (640,262), (771,357), (721,512), (559,512), (509,357) - and a frame taken with it resting there. A DIFFERENT WEDGE IS LIT IN EVERY TILE, and it is the one under the cursor: TURRET, then SHIELD, then RADAR, then REPAIR REACTOR, then UPGRADE SHIP. The seam agrees at every step: the selected flag moves 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 and is never on two wedges at once. PHONE 798x384, BOTTOM STRIP: a tap is a down and an up, and my first five phone frames were all taken after the up, so all five showed nothing lit - that was a hole in the capture, not a finding about the phone, and these frames close it. The touch is dispatched as a `touchStart` and HELD across the shutter, released afterwards. Under the held finger TURRET, SHIELD, RADAR and REPAIR REACTOR each light in turn; the fifth tile shows the UPGRADE wheel (WEAPON / HULL / ENGINE / CARGO), because pressing UPGRADE SHIP is what its `OPEN` does. The seam reports the selection following the finger and returning to nothing on release - momentary on touch, sticky under a pointer. ONE MARK THAT DOES NOT MOVE, NAMED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR A STUCK CURSOR: a small white diamond sits on the rim at twelve o'clock in all ten tiles. It is the index mark for where segment 0 begins; it is fixed by design and it stays put while the highlight walks past it. ALSO VISIBLE: as the sweep builds things the counts advance (`0/4` -> `1/4`, `0/2` -> `1/2`, `0/1` -> `1/1`), and once RADAR reaches `1 / 1 BUILT` its cost line stops quoting 6 and reads the word FULL.

title: With the wheel up on a phone the pause plate is withdrawn; the hub's CLOSE answers a real tap, but a tap where pause stood dismisses the wheel instead of pausing
attestation: THE VERDICT IS `verified` BECAUSE THE WAY OUT WORKS - nothing here traps a player - and the pause behaviour underneath it is described exactly and left for the Director to rule on. PRODUCTION BUNDLE, ?debug=1, phone 798x384. WHAT THE CLIENT DRAWS. With the wheel SHUT the layout registry lists `pause-button` at logical (72,16) 48x48 and the frame shows a pause plate there. The frame the wheel OPENS, `pause-button` is not in the list at all and the top-left of the plate's first tile carries `ORE` and `6` and nothing else. This is a0-96's shape of question - an affordance that is not where a player left it - so it was pressed rather than argued about. PRESS 1, THE HUB. `document.elementFromPoint` at page (399,192) - the centre of the `wheel-hub-back` rect the client reported - returned the CANVAS, so nothing was over it. A real tap there: the wedge readback went from five wedges to none, the frame shows the wheel gone, and the pause plate is back at the top-left. CLOSE ANSWERS A FINGER, and the hub on this profile correctly says `CLOSE` rather than the desktop's `CLOSE . ESC`. PRESS 2, WHERE PAUSE USED TO BE. With the wheel re-opened, `elementFromPoint` at (96,40) also returned the canvas, and a real tap there CLOSED THE WHEEL AND DID NOT PAUSE: the client reported screen `closed` before the tap and `closed` after it, and the third tile shows the match running with the pause plate back. So a phone player who reaches for pause while the wheel is up spends that tap dismissing the wheel and must press a second time. PRESS 3, THE DESKTOP KEY. A real Escape with the wheel up closes the wheel and does not open the pause overlay (five wedges before, none after, screen `closed` throughout) - the same precedence, stated by the hub's own label.

title: On the phone profile the onboarding prompt is drawn across the build wheel's lower disc - 318 logical px of overlap, on the front door and under ?debug=1 alike
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, phone 798x384, on BOTH boots. WHAT IS VISIBLE: with the build wheel open, the sentence `Be the last station standing - mine ore, build defenses, upgrade your ship, attack when you judge it right` is set in three lines across the bottom of the screen, and its first two lines are drawn over the wheel's lower disc, crossing the REPAIR REACTOR and RADAR wedges. The prompt's white accent bar, at the left of the band, starts inside the wheel's bounding box. THE ARITHMETIC, from the client's own layout registry: `onboarding` occupies logical (232.9, 309) 332.2x59 and `build-wheel` occupies (239.7, 32.7) 318.5x318.5 - an intersection 318.5 px wide and 42.3 px tall, which is the WHOLE WIDTH of the wheel. THE WORDS REMAIN LEGIBLE in this frame - white type on the wheel's mid-grey disc, with no glyph of the wheel's own copy struck through; the nearest wheel text, RADAR's `0/1 BUILT`, clears the prompt's first line by about 20 logical px. What is wrong is that two owned surfaces are sharing pixels with nothing arbitrating, on the narrowest supported width, where any longer prompt has nowhere to go but further up the wheel. THE DESKTOP PROFILE DOES NOT COLLIDE: at 1280x800 the wheel's registered box ends at y=665 and the prompt starts at y=709, 44 logical px clear, and the desktop overlap list contains no onboarding/build-wheel pair. So this is a narrow-viewport failure, not a design that overlaps everywhere. IT IS NOT AN ARTEFACT OF THE DEBUG BOOT: the second frame on the plate is the ?debug=1 capture and the first is the front door, and they collide identically.

title: The match HUD at rest, front door, with all five elements the brief names - including the desktop's missing pause affordance and the phone's missing controls strip
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, FRONT DOOR (/?gate=0 -> PLAY -> PLAY SOLO -> RUSH), no ?debug=1, about five seconds into a real offline match with seated bots. THE ORE COUNTER: top-left, the word ORE over a yellow `3`, with a thin rule under it. THE SHIP HP: THERE IS NONE ON EITHER FRAME. The only hull readout on screen is the STATION's - `100/100 HOME` with a blue bar, top-right. The ship's own HP is a bar drawn over the ship only once it is damaged (see the under-attack entry), so at full health a player has no ship-HP readout anywhere; this is deliberate, the dedicated top-right HULL element having been removed on an earlier field report, and it is recorded here because the brief asked for ship HP and this is what a resting HUD offers. THE MINIMAP: bottom-right on both, a dark panel with one clipped corner and a fog circle carrying the player's arrow. THE CONTROLS STRIP: desktop only, along the bottom - `Click anywhere Move or attack E Build & Upgrade`. There is no strip on the phone. THE PAUSE AFFORDANCE: phone only - a plate with a pause glyph at the top-left, immediately right of the ore counter. THE DESKTOP HAS NO PAUSE AFFORDANCE DRAWN AND ITS CONTROLS STRIP DOES NOT NAME ONE; Escape does open the pause overlay (pressed, below) but nothing on the screen says so. ALSO ON THE PHONE FRAME: a `VIEW 1x` zoom control under the station bar, a round BUILD & UPGRADE button at the left, and NO thrust stick and NO fire button - the default scheme is tap-to-command, so BUILD, pause and zoom are the only on-screen controls. THE PAUSE PRESS: on the phone, a real tap at page (96,40), the centre the client reports for its pause button - `elementFromPoint` returned the canvas, screen went `closed` -> `menu` and the sim froze. On the desktop, a real Escape - same result. Both overlays draw RESUME / SETTINGS / EXIT TO MENU with DOWNLOAD LOG alone in the bottom-right corner, clear of all three plates (a0-97's fix, holding on this screen). WHAT THESE TWO FRAMES DO NOT SHOW: any combat. The bots did not engage inside the window.

title: The HUD under a staged siege: a red frame, the station bar at 88/100 with a red arc on the ring, rival bars with numbers, and the ship's own HP as a bar reading 23/50
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, ?debug=1. THE DAMAGE IS STAGED AND I SAY SO PLAINLY: it is applied through the sim's own damage functions (`damageShip` / `damageCore` and the health-bar stage), because spec 5 flew the ship out and shot for twenty seconds and the bots never engaged, which produced an honest picture of an empty starfield and no answer to the brief's 'mid-fight'. NOTHING ABOUT THE HUD IS STAGED - no element is shown, hidden, moved or armed by the harness; it hurts things and photographs what the shipped HUD did about it. WHAT IS VISIBLE ON BOTH PROFILES: a red frame runs round the entire viewport. The top-right reads `88/100 HOME` with the bar part-empty. A RED ARC has appeared on the player's own station ring at the bearing it was hit from. The onboarding band has changed to `Your station is under attack - Follow the arrow`. On the phone the pause plate is still drawn - the alarm does not withdraw it. THE DESKTOP FRAME ALSO CARRIES RIVAL HEALTH BARS WITH NUMBERS - `Warden (HARD) 49/55` in blue and `Sable (HARD) 35/35` in orange, each under its nameplate, each over its ship. THE SHIP HP, which the resting HUD has no readout for, appears here as a bar above the local ship reading `23/50` (third block, a 3x crop). Its numerals are drawn across the station's bright blue ring and lose contrast against it. TWO THINGS THIS FRAME COST ME AND ARE WORTH RECORDING FOR WHOEVER CAPTURES NEXT: the queued `damageCore` write does not reliably land on one call - the first run of this spec left the desktop core at 62 and the phone core at 100 from the same call, and a re-run with nothing but that call left BOTH at 100 - so the harness now repeats it until the core actually moves and writes down how many tries it took (one, on both, this time). The same is true of `damageShip`, whose 45 points never landed at all; the 23/50 above came from the health-bar stage's own `damageLocal`. That is a statement about the debug seams, not about anything a player can reach.

title: The station bar and the ship bar are drawn seconds apart on the same screen and drain in opposite directions
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, desktop 1280x800, both crops from the same match minutes apart, at 3x. THE STATION BAR at `88/100`: the missing twelve per cent is an EMPTY DARK BLOCK AT THE LEFT END of the bar and the blue fill is anchored to the RIGHT. It empties leftward. The arithmetic is right - the dark block measures about 11 per cent of the bar's length - so this is a statement about the anchor and not about the value. THE SHIP BAR at `23/50`, drawn over the local ship in the same match: the blue fill is anchored to the LEFT and the empty part is at the RIGHT. It empties rightward. TWO HULL READOUTS, ONE SCREEN, OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. A player who has learned to read one at a glance has learned the wrong thing about the other, and `88/100` and `23/50` are the same kind of number about the same kind of thing. I am not ruling on which one is correct: the station block is right-aligned under a right-aligned `HOME` label, so a right-anchored fill there is arguable, and the ship bar's left anchor is the ordinary convention. What is not arguable is that they disagree. RIVAL SHIP BARS ON THE SAME FRAME - `Warden (HARD) 49/55` - use the SHIP convention, fill anchored left, so the station bar is the odd one out of three and not one of two.

title: The ore counter has no plate behind it: on this frame it sits on an asteroid, with a yellow ore crystal and a gold vein ring beside its own yellow numeral
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, top-left corner of both profiles at 2x, taken from the under-attack frames (hence the red alarm border at the crop edges). WHAT IS VISIBLE: THE ORE COUNTER HAS NO PLATE, SCRIM OR PANEL BEHIND IT - the word ORE, the numeral, and a thin underline rule are drawn straight onto whatever the world put there. On the desktop tile an asteroid has drifted under it. The result: the counter's thin rule runs across grey rock and is very nearly invisible for its whole length; and the asteroid carries a YELLOW ORE CRYSTAL and a GOLD VEIN RING within a few tens of pixels of the counter's own SIGNAL-YELLOW numeral - the same hue, at a similar size, with nothing separating them. THE COUNTER IS STILL READABLE IN THIS PARTICULAR FRAME, and I want that stated rather than glossed: what it has is no guarantee that it will be, and the thing most likely to drift under a counter that reads ore is a rock with ore on it. The phone tile shows the same counter over plain starfield with its rule fully legible, which is what the element looks like when the world happens to cooperate; an asteroid sits just below it in that frame. EVERY OTHER CORNER ELEMENT ON THESE FRAMES IS IN THE SAME POSITION - the station bar, the wave clock and the zoom control are all drawn without backing - but the ore counter is the one whose colour the world also uses. RELATED, SAME CLASS, SMALLER: on the desktop at-rest frame the build stamp `fabe6c3*` at the bottom-left is partly crossed by an asteroid.

title: The phone minimap stops 132 logical px short of the right edge - a sixth of the screen - while every other right-hand element hugs a 16px margin, and the anchor check passes anyway
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, both crops taken out to the true screen edge at 1x, at rest. THE NUMBERS ARE THE CLIENT'S OWN, off the layout registry. PHONE 798x384: `minimap` occupies logical (586, 292) 80x80 in a 798x384 viewport, so it ends 132 px from the right edge and 12 px from the bottom. The crop shows exactly that - an expanse of empty starfield to the right of the panel about a sixth of the screen wide. EVERY OTHER RIGHT-HAND ELEMENT ON THAT PROFILE HUGS A 16 PX MARGIN: `station-hp` ends at 782.5 and `zoom-control` at 782, of 798. DESKTOP 1280x800: `minimap` occupies (1120, 600) 148x148 in 1280x800 - 12 px from the right edge and 52 from the bottom. It is in its corner. So the same element, declared to the same `bottom-right` anchor, sits 12 px off the right edge on one profile and 132 on the other. NOTHING IS DRAWN IN THE GAP. If the space is being kept for a thumb, this scheme has no thumb controls to put there: the registry lists no `touch-fire-button`, no `touch-left-stick` and no `touch-aim-stick` on this profile, because the default scheme is tap-to-command. AND THE CHECK THAT EXISTS TO CATCH THIS DOES NOT CATCH IT: `placement()` - the registry's own 'is it inside the region it declared' test - returns ok for the minimap on BOTH profiles, because the `bottom-right` zone it tests against is the entire lower-right quadrant. That is part of the finding, not an excuse for it.

title: The under-attack prompt tells the player to follow an arrow while their station is already centred on screen and no arrow is drawn on either viewport
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, ?debug=1, the staged siege, both viewports at the same moment. WHAT IS VISIBLE: the onboarding band reads `Your station is under attack - Follow the arrow`. The player's own station is the large lit object at the centre-right of that very frame, labelled YOU, with the red damage arc on its ring. THERE IS NO ARROW ON EITHER FRAME. I went looking rather than concluding: the one candidate mark, on the desktop frame's left edge, is on this plate at 3x and magnifies into Sable's fighter beside the red alarm border. THE READING I CANNOT MAKE FROM THESE FRAMES, stated so nobody takes the verdict for more than it is: if the screen-edge arrow is meant to appear only while the station is OFF screen, then the arrow is absent correctly and what is wrong is the sentence - it is being shown in the one state where what it names cannot be followed. If the arrow is meant to be up whenever the alarm is, it is missing. Either way a player reading this prompt on this frame is told to follow something that is not there. WHAT I DID NOT CAPTURE: the same alarm with the station off screen. Both sieges were staged with the ship parked at its own station, so I have no frame of the arrow doing its job, and I cannot say from this evidence that the arrow is ever drawn at all.

title: The reachability audit: every pressable HUD control answers at its own centre on both viewports, and the three registry collisions that remain are named for what they are
attestation: PRODUCTION BUNDLE, ?debug=1, both profiles, wheel shut and wheel open. THE METHOD IS a0-96's: every element the client drew was intersected with every other, and every pressable element's own reported centre was handed to `document.elementFromPoint` - the browser's answer to 'who gets this press', which is what found the covered DONE plate. THE RESULT: EVERY PRESSABLE CENTRE RETURNED THE CANVAS, in all four states. Phone `pause-button` (96,40), `build-button` (92,172), `zoom-control` (750,85), `minimap` (626,332); desktop `minimap` (1194,674). There is no DOM element over the match HUD at all - the whole document is `div#app` and the canvas - so a0-96's class of bug is not present on this screen. THE ONLY CONTROL THAT DOES NOT ANSWER IS ONE THAT IS NOT DRAWN: `pause-button` is absent from the phone's element list whenever the build wheel is open, which is written up in its own entry. WHAT DOES INTERSECT, AND WHY NONE OF IT IS A COLLISION. `banked-total` inside `ore-hud` on both profiles - the number inside its own counter. `build-badge` and `controls-strip` on the desktop, 43.5x6 logical px - the build stamp against the NOMINAL 40px strip band, and on the frame the stamp sits clear above the strip's words with no glyph touching. `ship-local` inside `build-wheel` and `wheel-hub-back` when the wheel is open - the wheel is centred on the ship, by design. THREE READINGS THAT LOOK LIKE FINDINGS AND ARE ARTEFACTS OF THE INSTRUMENT, named so no one else spends an afternoon on them: `nameplates` and `healthbars` are each ONE UNION RECT around every plate or bar on screen (the desktop union is 627x575 logical at rest), so their intersections are not per-plate claims and I checked the frames rather than the rectangles - no individual nameplate is under the wheel on either profile; and `alarm-frame` is a full-viewport element, so under attack it intersects every other element by construction. THE ONE REGISTRY INTERSECTION THAT IS REAL is `onboarding` x `build-wheel` on the phone, which has its own entry.
